title: OSCI Pro — Charisma Quadrant Assessment
subtitle: Sixty questions. About ten minutes. Answer honestly, the way you actually are at work, rather than the way you would like to be. The honest answer gives you the most useful report.

items.text: I feel settled in myself, regardless of how recent events have affected me.
When I do something well, I take it as positive feedback on my skills and effort, rather than waiting for someone else to confirm it.
My sense of how well I am doing depends on the feedback I receive from peers, colleagues and friends.
When something goes badly, I can separate the incident from a general verdict on who I am.
When I am criticised, I start to doubt my skills, my identity, and my track record.
When a situation starts going wrong, I slow down and think about why, rather than push on without changing anything.
After a setback, I can usually identify something I can act on within the next couple of days.
When I am under pressure, I lose track of what the people around me actually need.
I can stay calm in a difficult conversation, even when I feel anxious inside.
After something has gone wrong, it tends to occupy my thinking for the rest of the day.
When I think a discussion is heading towards a poor decision, I say so before the decision is made.
When I make a commitment, I am specific about what I will do and by when.
When I disagree with someone whose opinion of me matters, I usually keep it to myself.
When something I am responsible for goes wrong, I tell the people affected before they find out from someone else.
I soften difficult messages so much that the main message gets lost.
When I am shown evidence I was wrong about something, I am comfortable saying so out loud.
In the last six months, I have asked someone for feedback that might be uncomfortable to hear.
When something I am doing is not working, I push harder at it rather than try a different approach.
In the last three months, I have chosen to do something that stretched me beyond what feels easy.
When I describe a weakness of mine, I treat it as something fixed about me, rather than something I am working on.
When an interaction goes wrong, I usually understand my responsibility for it.
Before a significant conversation, I take a moment to notice the state I am in, physically, emotionally and mentally, and decide how to handle it.
Feedback from other people usually matches the way I would describe myself.
I notice when my energy or focus has dropped before it affects how I am with other people.
The way I think I come across to other people is usually the same as how they actually see me.
When someone is telling me something difficult, I let them finish before I respond, even when I think I know what to say.
In a conversation, I can usually tell when the other person is troubled by something even if they have not said it out loud.
I usually have my response ready before the other person has finished speaking.
When someone brings me a problem, I check what they want from the conversation before I start solving it.
After a difficult conversation, I find it hard to identify what the other person was most worried about.
In social and work situations, I tend to greet or acknowledge everyone I see, whether or not I know them.
When I see someone I have met before, I can usually remember something specific about them.
The amount of attention I give people depends on how useful they are to me.
I follow up with people after a conversation that mattered, even when there is no task attached.
I show more warmth and interest to people who are important to me than to people who are not.
In a conversation, my follow-up questions are usually linked to what the other person has said, rather than the topic I had in mind.
When I meet someone new, I find out something about them beyond what they do for a living.
In conversation, I bring up my own experience before I have fully heard the other person's.
When I share an opinion, I usually frame it as my point of view rather than as a fact.
The version of me people meet in casual conversation is noticeably different from the version they meet in formal settings.
When someone disagrees with me in front of others, I stay calm in how I feel, what I say, and how I look.
When I am praised for something that involved someone else's work, I name their contribution in the moment, not later.
When I do not know something, I avoid admitting it directly.
When I am the most senior or experienced person in a group, I let others speak before I share my view.
I behave more carefully in front of people I want to impress than I do with everyone else.
I treat the most junior person in a group with the same quality of attention as the most senior.
I behave differently when I know I am being observed than when I think I am not.
People who know me at work and people who know me outside it would describe me in the same terms.
When I am tired or distracted, my warmth and attention drop noticeably.
My warmth and attention are the same whether or not the person can do something for me in return.
Before an important conversation, I decide the one thing I most need the other person to take away.
When I have something important to say, I can identify the most important thing that I want the other person to understand.
When time is short, I try to include everything rather than focus on what matters most.
I add impact to messages, with examples or vivid images in words, rather than leaving them more abstract.
When I am trying to explain complex things, my main point sometimes gets lost in the details.
When I want an important message to land, I add verbal and non-verbal emphasis to help get the point across.
I can read the room as I speak, and change what I am doing if my message is not landing.
I am comfortable leaving a moment of silence after making an important point rather than filling it with words.
Under pressure, I become less clear in the way that I speak.
My speaking style lacks energy and expressiveness.

consistencyBands.label: Charismatically adaptable
consistencyBands.description: Your warmth and attention show up reliably across the audiences and situations in your life. The surface adapts to who is in front of you; the underlying disposition does not.

consistencyBands.label: Broadly adaptable
consistencyBands.description: Your warmth is dependable in most settings, with one or two specific contexts where the fuller version of you narrows. The work is to identify those contexts and bring the same quality of attention there.

consistencyBands.label: Context-specific
consistencyBands.description: Your warmth is real, and unevenly distributed. The people closest to you get the full version. People at the fringes of your life get less. The development opportunity is to widen the reach of what you already have.

consistencyBands.label: Highly context-specific
consistencyBands.description: Your warmth is strongest when the context calls it out, and less reliably available elsewhere. The pattern is not unusual, and the work to widen it is direct: keep deploying the warmth you have, in the places it does not yet reach by default.

incidentally_invisible.label: The Incidentally Invisible
incidentally_invisible.tagline: Talented but overlooked. Ability is not the gap. Visibility is.

unknowingly_influential.label: The Unknowingly Influential
unknowingly_influential.tagline: Connects naturally. Undersells consistently. Influence outruns reputation.

occasionally_overconfident.label: The Occasionally Overconfident
occasionally_overconfident.tagline: Commands attention. Loses the room when warmth or restraint is the test.

courteously_charismatic.label: The Courteously Charismatic
courteously_charismatic.tagline: Competent and connected. The work is consistency. Closing the gap between best and average.

personalImpactBands.label: Lands reliably
personalImpactBands.description: The message gets through in most rooms, to most people, most of the time.

personalImpactBands.label: Lands in most rooms
personalImpactBands.description: The message gets through in familiar settings, with some loss in harder ones.

personalImpactBands.label: Inconsistent
personalImpactBands.description: The message gets through some of the time. Often the substance is there but the delivery loses it.

personalImpactBands.label: Not yet landing
personalImpactBands.description: The message is not reliably getting through, even when the underlying thinking is sound.
